I'll set up the parameters and confirm the block dimensions.

Now the blockMeshDict: three fluid blocks in x (so the middle one's bottom face matches the solid top face exactly → conformal interface), plus the recessed copper block below z=0. Cell zones `fluid` and `solid` are named on the blocks. Coarse 5 mm cells first.
Boundary faces, with orderings chosen for outward normals. Fluid bottom is wall only outside the block footprint; the middle bottom face is left internal (interface).
The trailing `}}` was in a plain string, not the f-string. Fix and rerun.
Mesh is right: bbox (0 0 −0.01)→(0.2 0.03 0.03), cell zones present. Now split into regions with a conformal interface.
Interface has 48 faces (8×6 cells = 40 mm × 30 mm). Now checkMesh on both regions.
Both regions clean. Now measure the actual patch areas and extents from the meshes themselves, and draw them.
Every number matches: inlet/outlet 30×30 mm, duct 200 mm, block 40×30×10 mm spanning x = 80–120 mm (centred at mid-length), interface at z = 0 with identical 1200 mm² on both sides. A look at it:
Shape is right: block flush with the floor, centred, conformal interface. Now refine to 2 mm cells by regenerating the dict (same topology, finer counts) and re-splitting.
Final verification on the refined mesh: checkMesh per region, plus re-measuring the patch areas and volumes.

Mesh is built and both regions are clean.

**What it is:** a block-structured hex mesh (no STL/snappy needed — the geometry is all right angles). Base mesh is four blocks: three fluid blocks in x spanning z = 0…30 mm, split at x = 80 and 120 mm, plus one solid block occupying x = 80…120 mm, full 30 mm width, z = −10…0 mm — the copper block recessed into the floor, its top flush with the duct floor. The middle fluid block's bottom face and the solid's top face share the same vertices, so `splitMeshRegions -cellZones` produced a genuinely conformal `fluid_to_solid` / `solid_to_fluid` pair (1500 faces, one-to-one).

**Measured against the request** (all in metres in the mesh; printed here in mm):
- duct cross-section: inlet and outlet patches each 900 mm² = 30 × 30 mm, at x = 0 and x = 200 mm.
- fluid volume 180 000 mm³ = 30 × 30 × 200 exactly.
- copper block: solid volume 12 000 mm³; extent x 80…120 (40 mm long, centred on mid-length x = 100), y 0…30 (full 30 mm width), z −10…0 (10 mm thick).
- interface: 1200 mm² = 40 × 30 mm on both sides, at z = 0.
- 2 mm cells: fluid 22 500 cells, solid 1500. `checkMesh` Mesh OK on both regions; non-orthogonality 0, skewness ~1e-13.

**Patches:** `inlet`, `outlet`, `fluidWall` (duct top, both sides, floor either side of the block), `solidWall` (block bottom, sides and both end faces), `fluid_to_solid`/`solid_to_fluid`. Each was named on the faces as they were constructed from block indices, not by bounding-box lookup.

**Not checked:** nothing about the solve — no `0/`, no thermophysical or `regionProperties` entries were written, so `chtMultiRegionFoam` needs its fields and material properties (copper) added before it will run. The stub `system/fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` exist only to let the mesh utilities load.
